title: Energy bills and the Autumn Budget 2026
subject: Household energy bills at forecast prices in 2026-27 and 2027-28 (the average extra cost against April–June 2026 cap rates), and the cost to government, reach and average gain of seven Autumn Budget 2026 energy support options: a Resolution Foundation-style targeted discount, a £100 Warm Home Discount top-up, a £300 Cost of Living Payment, £400 to every household, a cap freeze at April–June 2026 tariffs, keeping 0% VAT on domestic electricity through 2027-28, and moving the remaining Renewables Obligation and Feed-in Tariff levies to taxation.
search_terms: remaining levies off electricity bills cost

targeted_discount_flat.description: The dashboard's simplified Resolution Foundation discount: a flat £175 to every Great Britain household on a means-tested benefit or whose highest individual income is under £24,000, on annual income, with full take-up.

rf_targeted_energy_discount.description: The Resolution Foundation's Targeted Energy Discount: a discount on gas and electricity unit prices for households on means-tested benefits or whose highest individual income over the previous three months is under £24,000, funded from general taxation (Billing me softly; Hitting the buffers).

whd_top_up.description: £100 on top of the £150 Warm Home Discount, paid from taxation; the dashboard models it as £100 to every Great Britain household where anyone receives a listed means-tested benefit.

cost_of_living_payment.description: A £300 Cost of Living Payment to households on means-tested benefits, the 2022-24 design.

whd_recipients_payment_300.description: Good Energy's proposal: an additional £300 to the roughly 6 million Warm Home Discount recipients this winter.

flat_400.description: £400 off every household's energy bill, the 2022 Energy Bills Support Scheme design.

cap_freeze.description: Household energy prices held at the April–June 2026 price cap (unit rates and standing charges), the government paying suppliers the difference: an Energy Price Guarantee at the April 2026 level.

extend_vat_cut.description: VAT on domestic electricity in Great Britain kept at 0% through 2027-28 instead of returning to 5% on 1 April 2027 (SI 2026/987 sets 0% from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027).

remove_levies.description: The remaining 25% of the domestic Renewables Obligation and the Feed-in Tariffs moved from household electricity bills to general taxation.

remove_remaining_ro.description: The remaining 25% of the domestic Renewables Obligation moved from household electricity bills to general taxation: one of the two levies in the dashboard's option.

remove_fit.description: The Feed-in Tariffs moved from household electricity bills to general taxation: one of the two levies in the dashboard's option.

whd_increase_570.description: The Resolution Foundation's option of raising the Warm Home Discount payment by £570 (Power struggle, March 2026).

remove_wider_levies.description: More than the remaining Renewables Obligation and the Feed-in Tariffs moved from household electricity bills to general taxation: at least the Warm Home Discount as well, and for most producers every remaining levy (each producer's list is in its claim's reform_hint).
